For spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy with resection of the splenic vessels, it is generally recommended to rely on other collateral blood supply options rather than the short gastric arteries. The left gastroepiploic artery has been identified as the main collateral vessel for the spleen after a spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy, and studies have shown that this artery can provide adequate blood flow to the spleen despite its involvement in other areas.

In fact, the completion of the match suggests that the majority of surgeons do not rely on the short gastric arteries for their patients, and instead use alternative collateral pathways. This is because the left gastroepiploic artery has been shown to be a reliable source of blood supply for the spleen, even in cases where it is involved elsewhere in the abdomen.
